2294345.title: C-DAC and Geological Survey of India sign Umbrella MoU to Strengthen Geoscience, Mineral Exploration and Disaster Management through Next-Generation Technologies
2294345.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
C-DAC and Geological Survey of India sign Umbrella MoU to Strengthen Geoscience, Mineral Exploration and Disaster Management through Next-Generation Technologies
Partnership to leverage AI, High-Performance Computing and Advanced Digital Technologies for Earth Science Applications
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Geological Survey of India (GSI) signed an Umbrella Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in geoscience, mineral exploration and disaster management through advanced next-generation technologies.

The MoU was signed at Electronics Niketan, New Delhi, in the presence of Shri S. Krishnan, IAS, Secretary, MeitY by Shri E. Magesh, Director General, C-DAC and Shri Pradeep Singh, Additional Director General, Geological Survey of India (GSI).

The collaboration aims to combine C-DAC's High-Performance Computing (HPC) capabilities with GSI's geological expertise to address complex sub-surface exploration challenges through advanced digital technologies. The partnership envisages the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and HPC for processing large geophysical datasets, enabling high-resolution 3D subsurface mapping, predictive modelling for mineral targeting and cognitive processing of decades of unstructured geological records into a domain Large Language Model (LLM).

The collaboration will also support disaster mitigation through slope-scale landslide monitoring using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), development of early warning systems and studies on Glacier Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF). In addition, it aims to accelerate the discovery of critical minerals and Rare Earth Elements (REE), thereby contributing to India's economic security, supply chain resilience and technological self-reliance.

The ceremony was attended by Shri Sudeep Srivastava, Joint Secretary, MeitY; Shri Maneesh Khar, Deputy Director General, DGCO, GSI; Dr. Praveer Pankaj, Director, DGCO, GSI; Dr. Mukesh Verma, Director, DGCO, GSI; Shri Manoj Jain, Group Coordinator (R&D in IT), MeitY; Cmde Sandeep Wadhwa, Executive Director (Corporate & Govt. 2294324.title: Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries
2294324.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries
“Quality Statistics as Driver of Change”
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi

The two-day meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices (NSO) of BRICS Member Countries was concluded on 4th August 2026, at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India under the theme "Quality Statistics as a Driver of Change" aligned with the overarching BRICS theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability". The event brought together more than 350 participants including representatives from National Statistical Offices of BRICS, policy makers, academia, think-tanks, civil society organisation and technical experts.

 

During the 2nd day, the main technical Session-III on ‘Identifying Common Innovation Areas for Potential BRICS Collaboration’ included two presentations on the theme of Modern Survey Methods & Digital Data Collection were made. India and Egypt shared their experiences in using digital platforms for collection of survey and census data. India presented the experience and lessons learnt during the shift from Paper based survey to modern survey tools like e-SIGMA (e-Survey Information Gathering and Management Application) that is a Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) enabled platform, designed to integrate large-scale sample surveys into a cloud-based architecture. Egypt highlighted the use of geospatial technology in producing their official statistics. The importance of use of AI in survey implementations and more use of administrative data in a nuanced manner in conjunction with survey data was also emphasised.

Technical Session IV focused on strengthening macroeconomic and sectoral statistics, highlighting key strategies and progress made by BRICS member countries in strengthening macro-economic statistics. India presented its transition roadmap for implementing the System of National Accounts, 2025 (2025 SNA) and demonstrated effective use of administrative data in official statistics. China shared its progress and early practical experiences in introducing the 2025 SNA framework. Meanwhile, Brazil showcased the integration of alternative data sources particularly publicly available online data from expanding e-commerce and intermediary platforms emphasizing that non-traditional data can complement existing sources to significantly enhance quality of statistics produced by member countries in a rapidly changing technological landscape. Indonesia also presented its implementation plan to transition to 2025 SNA while also highlighting the adoption of ISIC 5 by them.

Along side the Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries 2026, the Ministry, in collaboration with the Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy, organized the side event titled "Building AI-Ready Public Data Systems in the Evolving Data Ecosystem". The discussions emphasized the importance of interoperable, trusted, and high-quality public data systems in enabling responsible AI adoption and supporting evidence-based governance. This side event featured a moderated roundtable discussion on the practical building blocks for AI-ready public data systems, followed by country case studies from India, South Africa, Russia, Indonesia, China, the UAE, and other partner organizations. Participants shared experiences on strengthening data governance, interoperability, metadata standards, institutional collaboration, and capacity building to transform fragmented data systems into AI-ready ecosystems. The deliberations highlighted the importance of international cooperation, knowledge exchange, and the adoption of best practices to build resilient public data systems that can effectively harness the potential of artificial intelligence for public good.

On the sidelines of the Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices (NSOs), the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, and BPS–Statistics Indonesia signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) during a bilateral meeting to strengthen cooperation in official statistics, capacity building, and strategic collaboration. The LoI provides a framework for collaboration in areas such as knowledge exchange, technological and methodological advancement, human resource development, and emerging areas including AI, metadata standardization, and open data.

The session concluded with adoption of the BRICS Joint Statement followed by concluding remarks session. The formal adoption of the Joint Statement marks a significant milestone in strengthening statistical frameworks across BRICS member countries, laying the groundwork for more robust, transparent, and policy-relevant official statistics. The Joint Statement may be accessed at  

https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1785840278403_a094383d-aeca-4106-a3d4-02fd91a2686e_Joint_statement_for_Meeting_of_Heads_of_NSOs.pdf.

2294315.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
IMPLEMENTATION OF NSAP
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Government is implementing National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) with an objective of providing a basic level of financial support to the most vulnerable sections of society - elderly persons, widows, divyangjan and bereaved households belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families. NSAP comprises five sub-schemes i.e. National Old Age Pension Scheme, National Widow Pension Scheme, National Disability Pension Scheme, National Family Benefit Scheme and Annapurna.

Under the scheme, eligible elderly persons, widows and divyangjan are provided financial assistance in the form of pension to supplement their means of subsistence and strengthen social security. In the event of the death of the primary breadwinner of a BPL household, one-time lump sum financial assistance is provided to the bereaved family under the National Family Benefit Scheme. Annapurna scheme provides food grains to senior citizens who though eligible are not receiving pension under National Old Age Pension Scheme. NSAP caters to 3.09 crore beneficiaries with a scheme-wise ceiling for each State/UT on the number of beneficiaries.

2294312.title: SARAS MELAS
2294312.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
SARAS MELAS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry has developed and launched the eSARAS platform, which serves as a dedicated digital marketplace for SHG products. In addition to facilitating direct sales through its own platform, eSARAS also enables the onboarding and sale of SHG products on other major e-commerce platforms.The State/UTs wise details of the registered SHGs/FPOs,etc. value and volume of sales  on the esaras platform including other major ecommerce platforms (Flipkart, Amazon, Meesho etc.) are provided as Annexure I.

As per the Ministry’s guidelines, all State Rural Livelihoods Missions may organize at least two SARASmelas annually in their respective States/UTs. In the financial year 2025-26, four national level melas have been organized with a cumulative sale of Rs. 35.73 crores. The State/UTs wise details are provided as Annexure II.

The eSARAS platform is a digital marketplace developed by the Ministry of Rural Development under the DeendayalAntyodayaYojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), in collaboration with the Digital India Corporation, to enable women-led Self Help Groups (SHGs), rural artisans and producer collectives to market their products nationally. To onboard more SHGs, FPOs, rural producers and strengthen their market access, the Ministry has provided digital onboarding support, including online product catalogues, inventory management and secure digital payment facilities. Women associated with SHGs are imparted training in digital onboarding, branding, packaging, product photography, digital marketing, customer service and product pricing. A dedicated Fulfilment Centre has been established to streamline the product collection, packaging, inventory management and last mile shipping of SHG products. The capacity building initiative focuses on digital marketing and facilitation of participation in selected business fairs and exhibitions to promote export ready SHG products. The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj regularly conducts capacity building and skill development programmes to support SHG members on product development, branding, packaging, quality improvement, digital marketing, enterprise management, export procedures and documentation, and market readiness to strengthen their access to domestic and international markets.

The Ministry regularly reviews the performance of the eSARAS platform and marketing initiatives, including SARAS Melas through sales reports and periodic consultations with States. The assessment indicates that these initiatives have significantly enhanced market access for women SHGs by connecting them with customers beyond their local markets through both physical and digital channels. SARAS Melas have provided SHGs with direct marketing opportunities, increased product visibility, facilitated interactions with institutional and retail buyers, and generated substantial sales, while eSARAS has enabled year-round online market access.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

OPERATIONALISATION OF SHE-LEAPS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Self-Help Entrepreneur-Livelihoods and Enterprise Application for Prosperity and Sustainability (SHE-LEAPS) has been operationalized and has the provision for monitoring the enterprises on boarded through SHE-LEAPS. The application was launched on 29th June, 2026 on the occasion of RashtriyaGraminVikasSammelan of Ministry of Rural Development. SHE-LEAPS application is developed under the LokOS digital platform for capturing enterprise-related information of Self Help Group (SHG) entrepreneurs under DAY-NRLM. The platform supports onboarding of enterprises and captures real-time enterprise data to facilitate management and monitoring of enterprises. It is being implemented across 34 States and UTs through the State Rural Livelihood Missions and in monitoring enterprises and support for planning and decision-making.

The State-wise details of SHG enterprises registered on the SHE-LEAPS digital platform are given at Annexure-I.

2294301.title: EMPLOYMENT UNDER VB-GRAM-G
2294301.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
EMPLOYMENT UNDER VB-GRAM-G
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi

Consequent upon commencement of the Viksit Bharat– Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025, the scheme has successfully been implemented in rural areas of the entire country w.e.f 01.07.2026. The VB-G RAM G provides for a statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty five days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work against one hundred day of guaranteed wage employment available under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The new scheme has been successfully implemented in the State of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh also w.e.f 0.1.07.2026.

In case of Maharashtra interim allocation Rs.4420.32 crore has been made for the State. Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.1459.92 Crore have been issued to the State of Maharashtra as first installment of Central Share under various components based on the proposal received from the State. Further in case of Madhya Pradesh an interim allocation Rs.6252.03 crore has been made for the State. Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.630.76 Crore have been issued to the State of Madhya Pradesh as first installment of Central Share under various components based on the proposal received from the State.

It is also stated that under Section 5(4) of the Act, the State Governments may make provision for providing additional days of employment beyond the period guaranteed under the Act from their own resources. The Act also aims to strengthen sustainable rural livelihoods through the creation of durable assets and implementation of the permissible works specified in Schedule I of the Act, namely Water-related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, Livelihood-related Infrastructure and Special Works to Mitigate Extreme Weather Events. These provisions are intended to enhance livelihood security, strengthen rural infrastructure and promote sustainable rural development.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), a flagship poverty alleviation programme of the Ministry of Rural Development, is being implemented through the State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) across 760 districts and 7,246 blocks in 34 States and Union Territories including Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. As of June 2026, the Mission has mobilized about 10.08 crore rural households into nearly 92 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs). Under the existing provisions of DAY-NRLM, capitalization support is provided to eligible SHGs in the form of Revolving Fund (RF) of ₹20,000–₹30,000 per SHG and Community Investment Fund (CIF) of up to ₹2.50 lakh per SHG to support income-generating and livelihood activities, including entrepreneurial ventures.

In addition, interest subvention is available on bank loans to eligible SHGs. For loans up to ₹3 lakh, banks provide credit at a concessional interest rate of 7% per annum. For loans above ₹3 lakh and up to ₹5 lakh, banks extend credit at an interest rate equivalent to their one-year MCLR or any other external benchmark-based lending rate or 10% per annum, whichever is lower. Cumulatively, loans amounting to ₹13.41 lakh crore have been disbursed to SHGs under the Mission. These benefits are available to eligible SHGs, including those in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, in accordance with the scheme guidelines.

 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

Ministry of Panchayati Raj
SVAMITVA SCHEME
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi

As on date, under the SVAMITVA Scheme, drone survey has been completed in 3.30 lakh villages across the country. Further, 3.24 crore Property Cards have been prepared for 1.97 lakh villages, about 2.72 crore Property Cards have been distributed to the property owners. State-wise and district-wise details are at Annexure-I

The main objective of the SVAMITVA Scheme is to provide a Record of Rights to property owners in rural inhabited (abadi) areas. The SVAMITVA Scheme is not integrated with eGramSwaraj, as eGramSwaraj is a work-based planning, accounting and monitoring system for Panchayats. To facilitate institutional credit on SVAMITVA Property cards, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Department of Financial Services and the State Revenue Departments are working collaboratively to enable wider acceptance of SVAMITVA Property Cards for bank loans. Some banks in States/UTs have started providing loans against SVAMITVA Property Cards. The State Governments are also utilizing the forum of the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) to streamline efforts for acceptance of these Property Cards by banks. 11,147 loans worth Rs 1,713 Crore have been disbursed based on SVAMITVA property cards. Among the said States, 2282 loan worth Rs.185 Crore have been availed on property cards in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. State-wise details are at Annexure-II.

Under the SVAMITVA Scheme, rural inhabited land is demarcated using drone survey and Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) technology to create high accuracy maps of abadi areas of villages. These highly accurate maps help reduce property-related disputes by clearly demarcating property boundaries and creating Record of Rights. Ministry is not aware of any major challenges related to property disputes, survey operations and public awareness. Furthermore, transparent process of ground verification and dispute resolution ensures that ownership records are finalized fairly and accurately. Ministry of Panchayati Raj provides funds to Survey of India for completion of drone survey and Maps preparation. Subsequent activities such as ground truthing, preparation and distribution of property cards are undertaken by States/UTs. Ministry of Panchayati Raj is continuously engaging with States/UTs and Survey of India for monitoring the progress of the Scheme and for timely completion of the Scheme to achieve its target of covering 3.38 lakh villages within the scheme implementation period.

2294295.title: SOCIO-ECONOMIC UPLIFTMENT OF RURAL WOMEN
2294295.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
SOCIO-ECONOMIC UPLIFTMENT OF RURAL WOMEN
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing Deendayal AntyodayaYojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY – NRLM) across the country (except Delhi & Chandigarh) with the objective of organizing the rural households into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and continuously nurturing and supporting them till they attain appreciable increase in income over a period of time and improve their quality of life. Cumulatively, 10.08 crore women have been mobilized into 92 lakh SHGs. The mission seeks to achieve its objective through investing in four core components, viz., social mobilization, promotion and strengthening of self-managed and financially sustainable community institutions of the rural poor; financial inclusion of the rural poor; sustainable livelihoods; and social inclusion, social development through its following sub-schemes.

i) National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM): A sub-scheme to promote sustainable institutions of the poor, their capacity building, livelihoods, ensuring access to financial services, strengthening social development outcomes such as Food, Nutrition, Health, WASH(FNHW) and gender inclusion

 

ii) Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP): SVEP is a sub-scheme under the DAY-NRLM, supports Self-Help Group (SHG) members and their family members in establishing small non-farm enterprises. The programme is implemented at the block level and as on May 2026, more than 6.5 lakh enterprises have been supported under SVEP.

 

iii) MahilaKisanSashakthikaranPariyojana (MKSP)-Under MahilaKisanSashaktikaranPariyojana (MKSP), which is another sub-scheme of DAY-NRLM aims at meeting the specific needs of women farmers to enable them to achieve socio-economic empowerment. The primary objective of the MKSP is to empower women in agriculture by making systematic investments to enhance their participation and productivity, as also create and sustain their agriculture-based livelihoods. The scheme also supports development of a pool of community resource persons to enable the community institutions to manage their activities.

 

iv) DeenDayalUpadhyayaGrameenKaushalyaYojana (DDU-GKY): DDU-GKY provides placement-linked skill training and employment opportunities in diverse sectors. Since inception (2014-15), it has trained 18.45 lakh rural youth including women and facilitated placement of 12.35 lakh candidates. Social inclusion remains at the core of the programme, with participation of 9.69 lakh women, 5.94 lakh SCs, 3.24 lakh STs, 3.12 lakh minorities and 0.14 lakh Persons with Disabilities.

 

v) Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI): RSETIs promote entrepreneurship and self-employment among rural households through short-term, demand-driven training and handholding support. RSETIs have trained 62.45 lakh candidates and successfully settled 45.25 lakh rural youth, largely through self-employment and micro-enterprises. Women constitute a significant share of beneficiaries, with 43.71 lakh (over 70%) women trained, alongside substantial participation from SC, ST, OBC, minority and PwD communities. The programme is supported by a robust network of 647 RSETIs across 634 districts.

 

The details of funds allocated, released/utilised under NRLM during the last five years, State wise, including Karnataka is given at Annexure-I. District-wise funds are not allocated under DAY-NRLM scheme.

 

The number of beneficiaries under DAY-NRLM scheme during the last five years, State wise and district wise including Chitradurga districts are given at Annexure-II and Annexure-III.

 

DAY-NRLM has undertaken focused initiatives for the inclusion and economic empowerment of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). The Mission prioritizes mobilization of vulnerable households into Self‑Help Groups (SHGs), strengthening of Village Organisations and Cluster Level Federations, and ensuring access to community investment funds, bank credit, livelihood promotion, skill development, and social security schemes. Emphasis is placed on tribal and socially excluded communities through targeted outreach in aspirational and tribal districts, dedicated capacity building, convergence with departments such as Social Welfare, and support for agriculture, livestock, non‑farm enterprises, and traditional livelihoods. These interventions have enhanced financial inclusion, women’s leadership, income generation, and access to entitlements among SC, ST, and OBC households, contributing significantly to poverty reduction and social inclusion across the country.

 

DDU-GKY is a placement-linked skilling programme for rural poor youth, and it explicitly prioritizes marginalized groups. The scheme mandates coverage norms of 50% for SC/ST, 15% for minorities, and 33% for women, and also gives special attention to women-headed households, persons with disabilities, and manual scavengers.

 

For women from SC/ST/OBC/EWS backgrounds can access free skill training, boarding and lodging, post-placement support, and employment-linked pathways without upfront training cost. DDU-GKY therefore serves as the main route for wage employment and career mobility for disadvantaged rural women with participation of 9.69 lakh women, 5.94 lakh SCs, 3.24 lakh STs, 3.12 lakh minorities and 0.14 lakh Persons with Disabilities.

 

Under RSETI, Women constitute a significant share of beneficiaries, with 43.71 lakh (over 70%) women trained, alongside substantial participation from SC, ST, OBC, minority and PwD communities. The programme is supported by a robust network of 647 RSETIs across 634 districts.

2294289.title: RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI SCHEME AND DEENDAYAL DISABLED REHABILITATION SCHEME
2294289.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI SCHEME AND DEENDAYAL DISABLED REHABILITATION SCHEME
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi

A third-party impact evaluation of the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) and the Deendayal Divyangjan Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS) has been conducted for their appraisal.

The evaluation study has reported that RVY is exceptionally well aligned with the needs of eligible senior citizens. The Scheme has had a transformative impact on the mobility and functional independence of beneficiaries by providing assistive devices that enable them to walk independently and move around without assistance. It is particularly effective in promoting independent living and reducing reliance on caregivers for basic mobility and daily functioning.

The evaluation study of DDRS indicates that the Scheme has delivered significant outcomes in education, rehabilitation, assistive support, and livelihood inclusion. It highlights the provision of educational and therapeutic services, leading to substantial functional improvement, along with the distribution of free assistive devices that have demonstrated high usability and beneficiary satisfaction. The evaluation also notes improved livelihood linkages, strong community and parental engagement, and enhanced transparency and timeliness through the e-Anudaan digital platform. Overall, the findings reflect high beneficiary satisfaction, improved social inclusion, and an enhanced quality of life.

This information is given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

2294287.title: CROP DIVERSIFICATION AND MICRO IRRIGATION
2294287.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
CROP DIVERSIFICATION AND MICRO IRRIGATION
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare has studied the prevailing cropping pattern and hydrological realities in different regions of India.  ICAR study using Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) data and monthly gridded GRACE satellite data indicated the mismatch between the water demand of existed cropping patterns and water availability in groundwater depleted states particularly in Punjab, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, encompassing the arid and semi-arid climates of the Country.  ICAR has also prepared ‘Atlas of cropping systems in India’ and also identified alternative cropping systems as sustainable alternatives to cereal-dominated systems considering the prevailing agro-climatic conditions, resource availability including water availability and market opportunities.

Further, ICAR has prepared the agro-ecological and district specific crop plan for 14 major crops namely rice, wheat, maize, pearl millet, sorghum, pigeon pea, chickpea, soybean, mustard, groundnut, cotton, sugarcane, potato and onion by combining the Relative Spread Index (RSI), Relative Yield Index (RYI), Sustainable Yield Index (SYI) and Soil-climate suitability index (SCSI).

Rice, sugarcane, cotton and jute are among the major water-intensive crops grown in India and together occupy about 62.7 million hectares, representing nearly one-third of the country's gross cropped area. Recognizing the need to align cropping patterns with local water availability, ICAR assessed the cultivation of major water-intensive crops in relation to rainfall and water availability. The assessment identified that about 2.89 million hectares of rice are cultivated in 68 districts receiving less than 650 mm annual rainfall, accounting for about 5.67% of the total rice area (51 million hectares).   Similarly, about 0.721 million hectares of sugarcane are cultivated in 91 districts receiving less than 700 mm annual rainfall, representing about 10.76% of the total sugarcane cultivated area (6.7 million hectares). These assessments provide the scientific basis for promoting location-specific crop diversification, particularly in water-scarce regions experiencing recurring water stress and declining groundwater levels, while balancing water security, farmer livelihoods and agricultural productivity.

The Government is promoting crop diversification from water-intensive crops to relatively low water-requiring crops such as pulses, oilseeds, millets and horticultural crops, taking into account local water availability, soil characteristics, agro-climatic suitability and sustainable use of natural resources. Under the Pilot Project on Crop Diversification, ICAR has implemented location-specific crop diversification interventions in 47 identified districts based on these criteria. To support diversified cropping systems, ICAR has also standardized and promoted optimum irrigation scheduling and drip fertigation for different crops to enhance water-use efficiency and productivity. Further, during 2023–24 to 2025–26, ICAR organized 457 training programmes, benefiting 8,749 farmers and 4,592 extension functionaries, to promote scientific crop diversification and sustainable crop management practices.

The Government is implementing several schemes and programmes to promote sustainable agriculture, micro-irrigation, soil health management and efficient utilisation of natural resources. The Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) promotes sustainable agriculture in 100 aspirational agricultural districts through convergence of interventions such as crop diversification, irrigation development, post-harvest infrastructure, natural and organic farming, Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM). The Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) promotes efficient use of irrigation water through adoption of drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. The Soil Health Card Programme promotes soil test-based balanced and integrated nutrient management by providing farmers with crop-specific fertilizer recommendations for improving soil fertility and nutrient use efficiency. Further, the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY (WDC–PMKSY 2.0) promotes integrated watershed management through soil and water conservation, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, restoration of degraded lands and sustainable management of natural resources.

In addition, ICAR promotes soil health management through soil test-based balanced and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM), Soil Test Crop Response (STCR)-based general fertilizer recommendations, and micronutrient mapping with location-specific nutrient recommendations. The Council has developed rapid and efficient soil testing kits and digital decision-support tools to facilitate timely soil fertility assessment and site-specific nutrient management. These technologies are disseminated through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), frontline demonstrations and farmer capacity-building programmes to promote balanced fertilization, improve nutrient use efficiency and sustain soil health.

The Government is promoting long-term water security and climate-resilient agriculture through research, technology development and field demonstrations led by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). The initiatives include rainwater harvesting, creation of farm ponds and other surface water storage structures, groundwater recharge, conjunctive use of surface and groundwater, multiple use of harvested water, in-situ moisture conservation, conservation agriculture, in-situ moisture conservation, protective irrigation, micro-irrigation, and AI-, sensor- and weather-based irrigation scheduling, and advisory systems to improve water-use efficiency and climate resilience,  and crop diversification from water-intensive crops to pulses, oilseeds, maize and agroforestry. ICAR also promotes micro-irrigation, Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), System of Rice Intensification (SRI), Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), raised-bed planting, laser land levelling, mulching, sprinkler and drip irrigation, and climate-resilient, water-efficient crop varieties through farmer training, frontline demonstrations, through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and State extension agencies.

The Government is strengthening the resilience of Indian agriculture to climate variability through research, technology development and field-level interventions complemented by flagship Government schemes. Under the National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA), ICAR promotes climate-resilient crop varieties tolerant to drought, flood, salinity and heat stress, Climate Resilient Villages (CRVs) in 151 vulnerable districts, District Agriculture Contingency Plans prepared for 651 districts, along with weather-based agro-advisories and farmer capacity building through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). These initiatives are supported through Government schemes such as the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) – Per Drop More Crop (PDMC), Watershed Development Component of PMKSY (WDC-PMKSY 2.0) and the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY), which improve resilience to climate variability and support environmentally sustainable agricultural practices. 

This information was given by Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2294288.title: PANCHAYAT DEVELOPMENT INDEX
2294288.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
PANCHAYAT DEVELOPMENT INDEX
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry has developed the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI), earlier known as Panchayat Development Index (PDI), as a composite assessment framework to measure the incremental performance of Gram Panchayats/Equivalent to Gram Panchayats across the themes of localization of sustainable development goals. The PAI provides theme-wise and overall scores through scorecards and dashboards, enabling identification of performance gaps, relative strengths, and areas requiring focused attention at the Panchayat level. A total of 2.59 Lakh Gram Panchayats/Equivalent to GPs of 33 State/UTs have been onboarded in the exercise of PAI 2.0 for FY 2023-24. State/UT wise numbers of GPs by overall PAI grades in 2.0 are placed at Annexure I.

Special incentive fund has not been created in the 2026-27 Budget for “Frontrunner” Panchayats in any themes of localization of sustainable development goals, including Theme 3: Child Friendly Village and Theme 4: Water Sufficient Panchayat.

The Ministry has been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) w.e.f. financial year 2022-23 with the major objective of Capacity Building & Training (CB&T) of Elected Representatives, Functionaries and other stakeholders of Panchayats across all States/UTs for enhancing the leadership skills and improving Panchayat Governance. Under the scheme of RGSA, the Ministry provides support for CB&T of elected representatives, functionaries and other stakeholders of Panchayats in different categories viz. basic orientation and refresher training, thematic training, specialized training, panchayat development plan training etc. A total of 36,81,750 elected representatives & other stakeholders of Panchayati Raj Institutions were trained on themes of localization of sustainable development goals (LSDGs) from FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27 (as on 10th July 2026) under the scheme. State/UT wise details of Thematic Training from FY 2022-23 to 2026-27 is placed at Annexure II.

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj facilitates the preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) through a thematic planning approach aligned with the nine themes of the Localization of Sustainable Development Goals (LSDGs). Gram Panchayats are advised to identify and prioritize key developmental sectors, referred to as “Sankalp”, before the preparation of their GPDPs.

Sectors related to climate-resilient agricultural practices viz efficient water management through drip irrigation & sprinkler systems, watershed development, agroforestry, and other sustainable agricultural practices, are integrated under Theme 4: Water Sufficient Panchayat and Theme 5: Clean and Green Panchayat.

For the Plan Year of FY 2026-27 (as on 29.07.2026), a total of 1,56,019 Gram Panchayats have taken Sankalp for the preparation of GPDP. Of these, 31,789 Gram Panchayats have selected Theme 4: Water Sufficient Panchayat and 32,806 Gram Panchayats have selected Theme 5: Clean and Green Panchayat as their respective focus areas.

No such collaboration has been established by the Ministry with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) under PAI.

The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) provide a globally accepted framework for sustainable and inclusive development. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has localized the SDGs for Panchayats by developing a framework of nine Localization of Sustainable Development Goals (LSDG) themes, making the global development agenda more relevant and actionable at the grassroots level. The localization of SDGs through the nine LSDG themes, supported by the PAI framework, facilitates effective rural governance, improved service delivery, and outcome-oriented Panchayat development.

2294282.title: UTILISATION OF FIFTEENTH FINANCE COMMISSION TIED GRANTS
2294282.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
UTILISATION OF FIFTEENTH FINANCE COMMISSION TIED GRANTS
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti is the nodal Department for the implementation of the Fifteenth Finance Commission Tied Grants. As reported by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, the Fifteenth Finance Commission submitted its report in two phases, the first, an Interim Report for the financial year 2020-21 and Final Report for the award period 2021-26.

The Fifteenth Finance Commission (FC-XV) recommended Rs.2.36 lakh crore to RLBs in 28 States including Andhra Pradesh for the period 2021-22 to 2025-26 including for those areas which are not required to have panchayats (Fifth and Sixth Scheduled areas and excluded areas), out of which 60% i.e. Rs. 1.42 lakh crore is tied grant to be utilized for (i) supply of drinking water, rainwater harvesting and water recycling; and, (ii) sanitation and maintenance of ODF status equally i.e. Rs. 0.71 Lakh crore for each component.

The release of tied grant allocated to all states is based on the fulfilment of stipulated criteria mentioned in the operational guideline for the implementation of XV-FC recommendation on RLB grants. Department of Expenditure further release funds to states and state government transferred the same to RLBs/ Excluded areas. The tied grant has to be utilized specifically for Water and Sanitation related activities as mentioned in the manual for utilization for tied grant.

Based on the interim report (2020-21) of the 15th Finance Commission, the entire recommended amount i.e. Rs. 1312.50 Crore was released to the State of Andhra Pradesh. Further, as recommended by 15th Finance Commission, year wise and State wise details of the allocation of Tied grant is enclosed at Annexure.

2294280.title: Indigenous African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine Developed by ICAR Bolsters India's Biosecurity
2294280.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Indigenous African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine Developed by ICAR Bolsters India's Biosecurity
Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, in the Presence of Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh, dedicates Vaccine to the Nation at this Year’s ICAR Foundation Day
A major step towards Atmanirbhar Bharat in veterinary vaccine development, with the potential to position India as a global supplier of affordable ASF vaccines
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

African Swine Fever (ASF), caused by the African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV), is one of the most devastating trans-boundary animal disease affecting domestic and wild pigs worldwide. Characterised by high fever, haemorrhages and mortality rates that may approach 100 per cent, the disease has caused severe socio-economic losses to the global pig farming sector. Since its first detection in India in 2020, ASF has spread to several States and Union Territories, resulting in massive pig mortality, disruption of pig production, restrictions on animal movement and trade, and significant livelihood losses for smallholder pig farmers, particularly in the North-Eastern region. In the absence of an effective treatment or a commercially approved vaccine in India, disease control has largely relied on rapid diagnosis, culling of infected animals and strict biosecurity measures.

The economic impact of ASF outbreaks in India has been significant. During the initial outbreaks in Assam in 2020 and 2021, pig mortality and culling resulted in estimated losses of approximately ₹276 crore. In Mizoram, ASF outbreaks have reportedly affected more than 11,382 households up to 2025, resulting in an estimated financial loss of approximately ₹982 crore. These outbreaks have highlighted the urgent need for an effective indigenous soultion to strengthen disease preparedness, protect farmers' livelihoods and build resilience in the country's pig farming sector.

Addressing this critical challenge, scientists at ICAR–National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal, have developed India's first indigenous MA-104_Cell_Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine for pigs. Developed using a novel attenuated ASFV Genotype II virus with unique gene deletions in the MA-104 cell line, the vaccine is a major breakthrough in veterinary research and is well suited for large-scale production.

The vaccine has successfully undergone comprehensive laboratory evaluation, including sterility, purity, safety, genetic stability, immunogenicity, protective efficacy and virulence reversion studies. It was also field validated in collaboration with the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, further establishing its safety and efficacy under field conditions. The vaccine is recommended for healthy pigs above eight weeks of age and is administered as a 1 mL intramuscular injection, followed by a booster dose 14 days after the primary vaccination.

The indigenous vaccine is expected to substantially reduce pig mortality, minimise economic losses and improve the livelihoods of pig farmers across the country. By providing an effective preventive tool against one of the world's most destructive livestock diseases, it will significantly strengthen India's animal health security and support the sustainable growth of the pig farming sector.

Dr. M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR said that this breakthrough marks the dawn of a new era in veterinary science. It reflects India's growing scientific capability to develop world-class animal health solutions and paves the way for a new generation of indigenously developed vaccines and innovative technologies that will strengthen livestock health, enhance disease preparedness, and support the nation's food and biosecurity.

At present, only a couple of commercially licensed ASF vaccines are available in Vietnam. These vaccines are produced using patented proprietary cell lines. In contrast, the indigenous vaccine developed by ICAR-NIHSAD uses the widely available MA-104 cell line, making it a major technological breakthrough. This eliminates dependence on proprietary manufacturing platforms, enables large-scale vaccine production and significantly brings down manufacturing costs.

2294278.title: Update on AB PM-JAY
2294278.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2294278.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Update on AB PM-JAY
As on 30 June 2026, AB-PMJAY Enables 12.69 Crore Cashless Hospital Admissions Worth ₹1.92 Lakh Crore, Reducing Out-of-Pocket Expenditure
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:12PM by PIB Delhi

Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) provides health coverage of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to 12 crore economically vulnerable families, constituting the bottom 40% of India's population. In March 2024, the scheme was expanded to include approximately 37 lakh families of Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi Workers, and Anganwadi Helpers. The scheme was further expanded in October 2024 to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status. The State/UT-wise details of Ayushman cards created can be accessed at https://dashboard.nha.gov.in/public/card

AB-PMJAY has significantly contributed in reducing out-of-pocket expenditure. As on 30.06.2026, a total of 12.69 crore hospital admissions amounting to Rs.1.92 lakh crore have been authorized under the scheme through a network of 37,413 public and private hospitals.

According to the National Health Accounts Estimates 2022-23, out of pocket expenditure as a proportion of total health expenditure declined from 62.6% in 2014-15 to 43.4% in 2022-23. This substantial reduction indicates that households are incurring a considerably lower share of healthcare costs directly from their own pockets, owing to increased public investment in health and the expansion of publicly financed health insurance schemes such as AB-PMJAY.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri. Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2294277.title: Update on NFHS-6
2294277.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2294277.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Update on NFHS-6
NFHS-6 Fact Sheet Indicators Finalised by Technical Advisory Committee in Line with Government's Data Harmonisation Initiative
NFHS-6 Fact Sheets Focused on Harmonised Key Indicators; Anaemia Estimates to Be Released Based on ICMR's Gold Standard Survey
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW) conducts an integrated survey namely National Family Health Survey (NFHS). The survey provides data on health and family welfare and associated domains like characteristics of the population; fertility and fertility preferences; family planning; maternal and child health; nutrition; morbidity and
healthcare; women’s empowerment, etc. The National and State/UT Fact Sheets of sixth round of NFHS (2023-24) were released on 29.05.2026.

The indicators to be included in the NFHS-6 National and State/UT Fact Sheets were ﬁnalized on the recommendations of the Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) constituted for NFHS-6, comprising representatives from concerned Ministries/Departments including Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Women & Child Development (MoWCD), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India (ORGI), NITI Aayog, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) etc.

The TAC recommended ﬁnalizing the list of indicators for the Fact Sheets in line with the Data Harmonization initiatives of the Government of India (GoI), so as to avoid inconsistencies arising from fragmented and unharmonized data available across diﬀerent oﬃcial data sources. The TAC further recommended that the Fact Sheets are intended to present only key indicators, particularly those related to health and family welfare, so as to better highlight the key takeaways of the survey.

Additionally, the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, after due deliberations, decided to adopt the prevalence figures of anaemia to be arrived from an independent survey conducted by Indian Council of Medical Research utilizing the gold standard intravenous method for haemoglobin testing.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2294276.title: Measures taken to strengthen 24×7 emergency services
2294276.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2294276.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Measures taken to strengthen 24×7 emergency services
As on 26 June 2026, 100% of Public Healthcare Facilities Assessed Through IPHS Digital Toolkit; 64% Score Above 50%
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

Public health and Hospitals are a state subject. The primary responsibility of strengthening public healthcare system lies with the respective States/Union Territories. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/ Union Territories to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural and underserved areas as per Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), based on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. States/ Union Territories are expected to ensure Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and Community Health Centres (CHCs) are functional with adequate staff, equipment, medicines and diagnostic facilities as per Indian Public Health Standards.

The details regarding doctors, specialists and paramedical staff in rural health facilities across States/Union Territories can be accessed at the following link of HDI 2023-24:

https://www.mohfwdohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac62.pdf

The Ministry has developed an open-source toolkit and a web-based dashboard (www.iphs.mohfw.gov.in) launched under IPHS on 28th June 2024 to facilitate self- assessment by all levels of facilities including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. The IPHS Dashboard is designed to monitor public health facilities' compliance with the IPHS 2022 standards and offers real-time updates, enabling oversight and data-driven decision-making to identify gaps and facilitate timely interventions.

As on 26th June, 2026, 100% of public healthcare facilities have been assessed through IPHS ODK toolkit. Out of total assessed facilities 64% of Health facilities have scored above 50% score.

Further, for strengthening 24x7 emergency services, obstetric care and diagnostic facilities in underserved rural areas, the Ministry’s support includes engagement of human resources, provision of essential drugs, diagnostics and medical equipment, infrastructure strengthening, establishment of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs), ensuring 24×7 services and First Referral Units (FRUs), implementation of the Free Diagnostics Service Initiative, Free Drugs Service Initiative, Biomedical Equipment Maintenance & Management Programme, National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) and other quality improvement initiatives.

This Ministry also supports ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM with the aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics services closer to the community, which in turn reduces the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE). Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities (14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111 test at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals).

For strengthening of Obstetric Care, comprehensive maternal healthcare services are supported under the National Health Mission (NHM), including antenatal care, institutional deliveries, skilled birth attendance, basic and comprehensive emergency obstetric care (including Caesarean section where indicated), postnatal care, referral transport, management of obstetric complications, and free maternal healthcare services under the Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) and Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), with the objective of ensuring safe motherhood and reducing maternal and neonatal mortality. 

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri. Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2294275.title: Measure undertaken to strengthen Health Research
2294275.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2294275.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Measure undertaken to strengthen Health Research
Government Enhances Health Research Funding; ICMR Budget Rises from ₹2,732.13 Crore in 2024-25 to ₹4,000 Crore in 2026-27
Government Strengthened Health Research Ecosystem Through New ICMR Funding Framework and Strategic Research Programmes
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi

Government has increased the budget in health research along with new schemes/initiatives to make research grants more competitive and accessible. The budgetary allocation for the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has increased from ₹2,732.13 crore in Budget Estimates 2024–25 to ₹3,125.50 crore in Budget Estimates 2025–26 and ₹4,000.00 crore in Budget Estimates 2026–27. The allocation for 2026–27 represents an increase of approximately 21 per cent over the Revised Estimates for 2025–26 of ₹3,150.00 crore.

The Government has also undertaken measures to broaden and strengthen the health-research funding ecosystem. ICMR has informed that it has rationalised and expanded its intramural and extramural grants architecture so that funding support is calibrated to the scale, maturity, risk and translational stage of a research proposal. ICMR has initiated new follow-on grants to utilize the leads from the initial research grants.

The current structure includes Small or ANVESHAN Grants of up to ₹2 crore, Intermediate or NISCHAYAK ANVESHAN Grants ranging from ₹2 crore to ₹8 crore, the First-in-the-World Challenge with stage-linked support of up to ₹8 crore, and Centres for Advanced Research with support of up to ₹15 crore. These instruments support investigator-initiated research, proof-of-concept studies, validation of interventions, high-risk and high-reward innovation, multidisciplinary research and advanced research programmes.

ICMR has further informed that it has initiated the following Strategic research funding grants to augment and supplement the research budget for public medical colleges and hospitals.

i) Top-Tier Global Leadership Funding Scheme: A flagship initiative to elevate global ranking of top-ten NIRF-ranked medical institutions as research leaders.

ii) ICMR–National Medical Commission (NMC) Joint Call: Research for Strengthening and Enhancing Quality of Medical Education by the top-100 NIRF-ranked medical institutions to support innovation and implementation research to enhance quality and outcomes of medical education with a focus on competency-based education, digital learning, and assessment reforms.

iii) ICMR Initiative for Strengthening Intramural Research in three Central Government Medical Colleges, Delhi.

iv) Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), in collaboration with ICMR and Gates Foundation, has launched the Mission for Advancement in High-Impact Areas (MAHA)-Medical Technology (महा MedTech). This landmark initiative aims to accelerate innovation in India’s medical technology sector, reduce reliance on high-cost imports, and promote equitable access to affordable and high-quality medical technologies.

v) ICMR Clinical Care Excellence Initiative: Multi-centre Clinical Trials addressing Non-Communicable Diseases

vi) Special Call for Proposals for Establishment of ICMR Centre for Advanced Research (CAR) for the Development of Priority Medical Devices and Diagnostic Technologies addressing unmet clinical needs identified by ICMR through extensive stakeholder consultations. The initiative seeks to promote the development of affordable, accessible, and indigenous healthcare technologies of national public health relevance for wider public benefit and long-term self-reliance in the MedTech sector. The priority medical devices and diagnostic technologies have been identified through a rigorous exercise involving eminent clinicians in different clinical settings across the country including clinicians from tier-1, tier-2 & tier-3 cities, resulting in a curated list of ~100 priority unmet clinical need based medical device/diagnostic technologies.

vii) ICMR’s Multistate Implementation Research Study to improve coverage of high-quality Palliative Care Interventions to develop, implement, and evaluate a scalable palliative care model integrated with healthcare services in India and to evaluate cost-effectiveness and feasibility of the model and generate evidence for national scale-up for palliative care.

ICMR supports several extramural research projects for frontier technologies including development of recombinant vaccines, biologics, cell and gene therapies, Robotics and AI-tools. 22 projects of frontier technology have been undertaken including CAR-T cell therapy & Robotics-based targeted therapy for cancer, cardiac massaging, root canal treatment. ICMR has further supported indigenous development of 97 medical devices/ diagnostic technologies and cost reduction for 11 technologies. Over 60 innovative projects have been supported in First in the World challenge.  

With a view to strengthen the domestic biopharmaceutical sector and enhance global competitiveness in biologics and biosimilars, the Government has announced the Biopharma SHAKTI scheme with an outlay of ₹10,000 crore over five years with an objective to build a globally competitive domestic ecosystem for biologics and biosimilars to support affordable healthcare in India and enable India to emerge as a global biopharma manufacturing and innovation hub. Further by supporting research and development, strengthening clinical trial infrastructure and promoting collaboration between academia, research institutions and industry, the Scheme seeks to encourage domestic innovation and manufacturing capabilities in the biopharmaceutical sector. Such initiatives are expected to contribute towards reducing import dependence over time and enhance India’s participation in the global biopharmaceutical market. The long-term goal is to move toward innovation leadership, including AI-designed biologics and advanced therapies and precision medicine to make these more affordable and accessible.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri. Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2294274.title: Update on NTEP
2294274.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2294274.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Update on NTEP
ICMR Study Finds Drone-Assisted TB Sample Transport Reduces Diagnosis Time from 15 Days to 5 Days and Patient Expenditure from ₹9,451 to ₹91
ICMR's i-DRONE Initiative Cuts TB Diagnosis Time by Two-Thirds and Reduces Patient Costs by Over 99%
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi

As per the latest study conducted by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) under its i-DRONE initiative, drone-assisted transport of tuberculosis (TB) sputum samples has been found to significantly reduce the time and cost of TB diagnosis in remote and hard-to-reach areas. The study, conducted in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana in collaboration with AIIMS Bibinagar and the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), demonstrated that the median turnaround time for TB diagnosis was reduced from 15 days to 5 days, while the mean out-of-pocket expenditure incurred by patients decreased from approximately Rs 9,451/- to Rs 91/-, thereby improving timely access to TB diagnostic services. 

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2294272.title: One Nation, One Fertilizer' Initiative Strengthens Fertilizer Availability and Distribution Across the Country
2294272.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers
2294272.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
One Nation, One Fertilizer' Initiative Strengthens Fertilizer Availability and Distribution Across the Country
Advance Planning, Digital Monitoring and Coordinated Supply Mechanism Support Timely Fertilizer Availability Nationwide
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has strengthened the country's fertilizer distribution system through the 'One Nation, One Fertilizer' initiative under the “Pradhanmantri Bhartiya Janurvarak Pariyojana” (PMBJP). Implemented with effect from 24 August 2022, the initiative mandates all Public Sector, Cooperative and Private Sector fertilizer companies to market subsidized fertilizers under the common “BHARAT” brand across the country.

The objective of the scheme is to increase the availability basket of fertilizers; take care of dilemma among farmers in choosing from plethora of brands manufactured by various companies available in the markets, reduce the crisscross movement and further ensure timely supply of fertilizers across the country. By consolidating branding under a single “BHARAT” brand, the scheme fosters transparency, combats malpractices, and ensures equitable access to essential nutrients for crops.  Presently, all the subsidized fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS grades are marketed under the Bharat Brand.

The Government has complemented the initiative with a robust fertilizer supply and distribution mechanism to ensure timely availability of fertilizers. Before the commencement of every cropping season, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with State Governments, assesses the State-wise and month-wise fertilizer requirement. Based on these projections, the Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers through monthly supply plans and continuously monitors their availability across the country.

To strengthen transparency and real-time monitoring, the movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is tracked through the Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS), an online web-based platform that monitors fertilizer movement across the supply chain. To bridge the gap between domestic production and demand, fertilizer imports are finalized well in advance to ensure timely availability during the cropping season.

The Government also regularly advises State Governments to coordinate with fertilizer manufacturers and importers for timely placement of indents and streamlined supplies. In addition, continuous coordination is maintained with the Ministry of Railways to ensure adequate availability of railway rakes, priority movement of fertilizers and timely evacuation of fertilizer consignments to various States. Distribution of fertilizers at the district level is undertaken by the respective State Governments.

In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS in the country has remained adequate during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. 2294268.title: PM-PRANAM Promotes Balanced Use of Fertilizer, Organic Farming and Natural Farming Across the Country
2294268.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers
2294268.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
PM-PRANAM Promotes Balanced Use of Fertilizer, Organic Farming and Natural Farming Across the Country
5 States/UTs Reduce Chemical Fertilizer Consumption Under PM-PRANAM in 2025-26
Government Expands Organic Farming, Natural Farming and Precision Nutrient Management to Improve Soil Health
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is promoting balanced and sustainable fertilizer use through the PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment and Amelioration of Mother Earth (PM-PRANAM), while simultaneously expanding organic farming, natural farming and precision nutrient management to improve soil health, reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers and promote environmentally sustainable agriculture.

Approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) on 28 June 2023 for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26, PM-PRANAM supports the mass movement initiated by States and Union Territories for balanced fertilizer use, adoption of alternative fertilizers, promotion of organic farming and implementation of resource conservation technologies. The scheme covers all States and Union Territories and provides incentives for reducing the consumption of chemical fertilizers, namely Urea, DAP, NPK and MOP, in comparison with the average consumption of the previous three financial years. The incentive is equivalent to 50% of the fertilizer subsidy saved, of which 95% is earmarked for the concerned State/UT and 5% is retained by the Government of India. Out of the State share, 65% is to be utilized for capital expenditure projects, preferably under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, while the remaining 30% is available for other activities, including Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives.

During 2025-26, 5 States/UTs namely Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Delhi, Goa, Manipur and Mizoram recorded a cumulative reduction of 0.18 Lakh Metric Tons in the consumption of chemical fertilizers (Urea, DAP, NPKs and MOP) compared with the average consumption of the previous three financial years. The Government has informed that incentives under the scheme have not yet been disbursed.

The Government has taken several steps to train farmers in precision farming techniques for the efficient and balanced use of nutrients and to promote the large-scale production of certified organic compost through various schemes of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The details are as follows:

Organic Farming (PKVY & MOVCDNER)

Organic farming is being promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) in the States/UTs and Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) for the North Eastern States since 2015-16. Both schemes stress on end-to-end support to farmers engaged in organic farming i.e. from production to processing, certification and marketing. Primary focus of the schemes is to form organic clusters, with preference to small and marginal farmers, to create a supply chain. Both the schemes are implemented through States /UT Governments. Under PKVY, assistance of Rs. 31,500 per ha is provided over 3 years for promotion of organic farming. Out of this, assistance of Rs. 15,000 per ha is provided to farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for on- farm /off –farm organic inputs. Under MOVCDNER, assistance of Rs. 46,500/ha is provided over 3 years for creation of Farmers Producer Organization, support to farmers for organic inputs etc. Out of this, assistance @ Rs. 32,500/ ha is provided to farmers for off -farm /on –farm organic inputs under the scheme including Rs. 15,000 as Direct Benefit Transfer to the farmers.

Under PKVY Scheme, since its inception (as on 30.06.2026), 18.93 lakh hectares area has been covered benefitting 33.63 lakh farmers and a total of ₹2811.36 crore (central share) has been released. Under MOVCDNER Scheme since its inception (as on 30.06.2026), 2.36 lakh hectares brought under organic farming benefitting 2.74 lakh farmers and a total of ₹1548.62 crore (central share) has been released.

National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)

The Government is also implementing the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), launched on 25 November 2024, to promote chemical-free farming integrated with livestock, diversified cropping systems and traditional Indian agricultural knowledge. The Mission has a total financial outlay of ₹2,481 crore, comprising a Central share of ₹1,584 crore and a State share of ₹897 crore, up to the 15th Finance Commission period (March 2026). Farmers adopting natural farming are eligible for an Output Based Incentive of ₹4,000 per acre per year for 2 years, limited to one acre per farmer.

`During FY 2025-26, 18,893 clusters covering 10.32 lakh hectares and involving 20.93 lakh farmers were formed under the Mission. To support field-level implementation, 33,257 Krishi Sakhis/Community Resource Persons (CRPs) have been trained and 7,601 Bio-Input Resource Centres (BRCs) established. In addition, 33.89 lakh farmers have been have been made aware about natural farming, 18.13 lakh soil samples have been collected and ₹599.68 crore has been utilized against a budget allocation of ₹725 crore during the financial year 2025-26. More than 22.47 lakh farmers have been registered under the Natural Farming Certification System (NFCS), of which over 14.43 lakh farmers have been certified.

To promote precision nutrient management, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed drip fertigation schedules for 50 crops covering 14 agro-ecological regions, which are being disseminated through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), frontline demonstrations, field demonstrations and farmer training programmes. ICAR has also standardized and promoted the use of Farm Yard Manure (FYM), phosphocompost, vermicompost, bio-enriched compost, municipal solid waste compost and enriched fermented organic manures through demonstrations, public awareness campaigns, training programmes and media outreach.

This information was provided by Smt. Anupriya Patel, Minister of State in the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha today.

Ministry of Finance
Government Boosts MSME Financing Through SIDBI and ECLGS 5.0
SIDBI Expands Nationwide Presence with 71 New Branches; Direct Credit Portfolio Grows 36.8% Y-oY
ECLGS 5.0 Envisages ₹2.55 Lakh Crore Additional Credit With up to 100% Guarantee Coverage for Eligible MSMEs
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

Some major initiatives have been undertaken by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) during the last five years to improve the flow of credit to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) across the country.

These include the following initiatives:

  1. Subsequent to Union Budget Announcement FY 2024-25, SIDBI has opened 71 new branches across India from 01.04.2024 to 29.07.2026 to expand its reach to serve major MSME clusters and provide direct credit to MSMEs.
  2. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s direct credit outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 51,687 crores, as against ₹ 37,781 crores as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 36.8%.
  3. The Bank also provides refinance assistance to augment resources of Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs) to increase their flow of credit to MSMEs. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s refinance outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 4,50,571 crore, as against ₹ 3,85,327 crore as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 16.9%.
  4. SIDBI has launched a product on co-lending arrangement with Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to provide affordable credit to smaller MSMEs, especially new borrowers, as part of its effort to reach underserved/ unserved MSMEs. During FY 202526, the Bank initiated co-lending arrangements with Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) to strengthen credit delivery and broaden financial access in underserved and untapped areas.
  5. Prayaas Scheme has been launched by SIDBI to facilitate access to affordable credit to informal micro-entrepreneurs/ micro-enterprises (IMEs), especially women and poor.
  6. SIDBI has launched a GST Sahay app for ‘on tap’ invoice-based (cash flow based) small value credit to micro enterprises using trade data and digital frameworks.

The Government has introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 in May, 2026. Under the scheme, MSMEs are eligible for additional credit up to 20% of the peak fund-based working capital outstanding during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26.

The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) towards the amount in default for such additional credit facility extended to the eligible MSME borrowers. For the scheduled passenger airlines, the guarantee coverage is 90%.

However, the scheduled passenger airlines are eligible for additional credit up to 100% of the total peak credit outstanding (both fund-based and non-fund-based) during the fourth quarter of FY 2025-26. Under the scheme, additional credit flow of ₹ 2,55,000 crore is envisaged for MSMEs, non-MSMEs and scheduled passenger airlines.  

This information was given by Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary in Rajya Sabha today.

2294255.title: INDIA AND UZBEKISTAN SHARE CENTURIES-OLD HISTORICAL, CULTURAL AND CIVILIZATIONAL TIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
2294255.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
INDIA AND UZBEKISTAN SHARE CENTURIES-OLD HISTORICAL, CULTURAL AND CIVILIZATIONAL TIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
INDIA–UZBEKISTAN PARLIAMENTARY FRIENDSHIP GROUP WILL GIVE FRESH IMPETUS TO BILATERAL RELATIONS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
H.E. MR. BAKHTIYOR SAIDOV, MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF UZBEKISTAN, CALLS ON LOK SABHA SPEAKER
Posted On: 04 AUG 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla observed today that India and Uzbekistan are bound by centuries-old historical, cultural, and civilizational ties that continue to provide a robust foundation for their enduring friendship. He expressed confidence that growing political trust, expanding trade and investment, and enhanced people-to-people exchanges will further strengthen the bilateral partnership in the years ahead. Shri Birla made these remarks during a meeting with H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Uzbekistan, who called on him at Parliament House. The two leaders held wide-ranging discussions on India–Uzbekistan relations, with a particular emphasis on parliamentary cooperation, trade and investment, education, culture, and issues of mutual regional and global significance.

Speaking on India's democratic traditions, Shri Birla stated that India, as the world's largest democracy, features a vibrant parliamentary system that effectively reflects the aspirations and diversity of its people. He noted that the 543-member Lok Sabha represents millions of citizens nationwide and that India's multi-party framework provides equal space for diverse perspectives and constructive debate. Referring to the functioning of the institution, Shri Birla informed the visiting dignitary that Parliament meets across three sessions annually, with the ongoing Monsoon Session actively deliberating on several matters of national importance.

Shri Birla highlighted India’s significant achievements in infrastructure development, digital innovation, technology, connectivity, investment and trade. He observed that India's youth are increasingly assuming leadership roles globally and that collaboration with leading universities and international institutions continues to expand. Referring to the India–Uzbekistan Parliamentary Friendship Group constituted in March 2026, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the initiative will impart fresh momentum to legislative engagement and deepen cooperation across economic, educational, cultural, and people-to-people spheres.

Recalling his participation in the 150th Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) held in Tashkent in April 2025, Shri Birla noted his interactions with H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, President of Uzbekistan; H.E. Ms. Tanzila Narbayeva, Chairperson of the Senate and Mr. Nuriddin Ismailov, Speaker of the Legislative Chamber. He observed that these high-level visits laid a strong cornerstone for ongoing parliamentary collaboration. Expressing satisfaction with the steady progress of bilateral relations, Shri Birla hoped that the current visit would further reinforce the comprehensive partnership between the two nations.

H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov reaffirmed Uzbekistan's firm commitment to deepening its multifaceted partnership with India, stating that Tashkent attaches high importance to expanding political, economic, and parliamentary cooperation. Appreciating India's robust democratic traditions, he noted that Uzbekistan stands to benefit significantly from the legislative experience of the world's largest democracy. Mr. Saidov further emphasized that enhanced parliamentary engagement will contribute meaningfully to advancing the comprehensive strategic partnership. He called for a shared vision to expand cooperation in trade, investment, joint projects, and emerging sectors.

To mark the occasion, H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov presented Shri Om Birla with a special commemorative publication detailing the 150th Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union hosted by Uzbekistan.

It was a pleasure to meet H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan, at Parliament House today.
